---
title: "Usage — 2D"
lightbox: true
---

The 2D model resolves constructive systems whose section is **not** a simple stack of
homogeneous layers: hollow blocks (`HollowBlock`, walls) and joist-and-block slabs
(`Slab`, roofs). [The workflow](usage.qmd) is the same as in 1D — the
differences are the class (`System2D`), that `tilt` must be `90` (`HollowBlock`) or
`0` (`Slab`), and that the 2D element goes **inside** the layer stack.

As in [Usage — 1D](usage-1d.qmd), the examples show **real results** for the average day of May in
Cuernavaca. Building the systems and inspecting their sections is executed live when
this documentation is rendered; the solves are **pre-computed** — a default-mesh 2D
solve takes ~10–20 minutes in a modern laptop — by
[`docs/run_examples.py`](https://github.com/Ener-Habitat/EnerHabitat/blob/main/docs/run_examples.py),
whose outputs (in `docs/data/results/`) this page reads and plots. Regenerate them
with `uv run docs/run_examples.py`.

## 2D geometries

The 2D elements — `HollowBlock` for walls, `Slab` for joist-and-block roofs — are
defined by a `geometry` dict (measures in **metres**). The schemes below name every
key, drawn to scale with the same values used in the examples further down
(shown in mm for readability):

```{python}
#| echo: false
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle

SOLID = "#a9c0e0"     # shell / filler block
RIB = "#5b83b8"       # joist (L-shaped rib)
TOPPING = "#7fa3cc"   # compression topping
AIR = "#dcefff"       # air cavity
DIM = "#374151"       # dimension lines and labels

def hdim(ax, x0, x1, y, label):
    """Horizontal dimension arrow with its parameter name below."""
    ax.annotate("", xy=(x0, y), xytext=(x1, y),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="<->", color=DIM, lw=0.9))
    ax.text((x0 + x1) / 2, y + 6, label, ha="center", va="top",
            fontsize=8, color=DIM)

def vdim(ax, y0, y1, x, label, side="right"):
    """Vertical dimension arrow with its parameter name beside it."""
    ax.annotate("", xy=(x, y0), xytext=(x, y1),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="<->", color=DIM, lw=0.9))
    dx, ha = (6, "left") if side == "right" else (-6, "right")
    ax.text(x + dx, (y0 + y1) / 2, label, ha=ha, va="center",
            fontsize=8, color=DIM)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
web, block_width = 20, 160                      # mm — same as the 2D wall example
cover_top, cavity, cover_bottom = 20, 80, 20
X = 2 * web + block_width
Y = cover_top + cavity + cover_bottom

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.2))
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((0, 0), X, Y, facecolor=SOLID, edgecolor="k", lw=1))
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((web, cover_top), block_width, cavity,
                       facecolor=AIR, edgecolor="k", lw=0.8, ls="--"))
ax.text(X / 2, cover_top + cavity / 2, "cavity (air or fill)",
        ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9, color=DIM)
ax.text(X / 2, -12, "OUTSIDE", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9, color="#b91c1c")
ax.text(X / 2, Y + 42, "INSIDE", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=9, color="#1d4ed8")

hdim(ax, 0, web, Y + 14, "web")
hdim(ax, web, web + block_width, Y + 14, "block_width")
hdim(ax, web + block_width, X, Y + 14, "web")
vdim(ax, 0, cover_top, X + 14, "cover_top")
vdim(ax, cover_top, cover_top + cavity, X + 14, "cavity")
vdim(ax, cover_top + cavity, Y, X + 14, "cover_bottom")

ax.set_xlim(-15, X + 95)
ax.set_ylim(Y + 55, -25)          # inverted: outside on top
ax.set_aspect("equal")
ax.axis("off")
ax.set_title("HollowBlock — geometry parameters (one cell)", fontsize=10)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
web, foot, shoulder = 25, 25, 50                # mm — same as the roof example
n_cavities, cavity_width = 3, 103
topping, topping_cap = 100, 50
cover_top, cavity, cover_bottom = 30, 40, 30
X = 2 * (web + foot) + (n_cavities + 1) * shoulder + n_cavities * cavity_width
Y = topping + cover_top + cavity + cover_bottom

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.0, 4.6))
# filler block body, then topping band, then the two L-shaped ribs on top
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((0, topping), X, Y - topping, facecolor=SOLID, edgecolor="none"))
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((0, 0), X, topping, facecolor=TOPPING, edgecolor="none"))
for x0, sign in ((0, 1), (X, -1)):
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((min(x0, x0 + sign * web), topping_cap),
                           web, Y - topping_cap, facecolor=RIB, edgecolor="none"))
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((min(x0, x0 + sign * (web + foot)), Y - cover_bottom),
                           web + foot, cover_bottom, facecolor=RIB, edgecolor="none"))
x0 = web + foot + shoulder
for c in range(n_cavities):
    xs = x0 + c * (cavity_width + shoulder)
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((xs, topping + cover_top), cavity_width, cavity,
                           facecolor=AIR, edgecolor="k", lw=0.8, ls="--"))
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((0, 0), X, Y, facecolor="none", edgecolor="k", lw=1))
ax.text(X / 2, topping / 2, "topping", ha="center", va="center",
        fontsize=9, color="white")
ax.text(X / 2, topping + cover_top + cavity / 2, f"n_cavities = {n_cavities}",
        ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9, color=DIM)
ax.text(web / 2, (topping_cap + Y) / 2, "rib", ha="center", va="center",
        fontsize=8, color="white", rotation=90)
ax.text(X / 2, -12, "OUTSIDE", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9, color="#b91c1c")
ax.text(X / 2, Y + 42, "INSIDE", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=9, color="#1d4ed8")

hdim(ax, 0, web, Y + 14, "web")
hdim(ax, web, web + foot, Y + 34, "foot")
hdim(ax, web + foot, web + foot + shoulder, Y + 14, "shoulder")
hdim(ax, x0, x0 + cavity_width, Y + 14, "cavity_width")
vdim(ax, 0, topping_cap, -14, "topping_cap", side="left")
vdim(ax, 0, topping, X + 14, "topping")
vdim(ax, topping, topping + cover_top, X + 14, "cover_top")
vdim(ax, topping + cover_top, topping + cover_top + cavity, X + 14, "cavity")
vdim(ax, topping + cover_top + cavity, Y, X + 14, "cover_bottom")

ax.set_xlim(-100, X + 110)
ax.set_ylim(Y + 60, -25)          # inverted: outside on top
ax.set_aspect("equal")
ax.axis("off")
ax.set_title("Slab — geometry parameters (one cell)", fontsize=10)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The rib is an **L**: its `web` rises through the whole element (stopping below the
full-width `topping_cap`) and its `foot` widens it only along the `cover_bottom`
band, forming the ledge the filler block rests on.

## Examples

Free-running and air-conditioned, for a hollow-block wall and a joist-and-block
roof. Setup shared by all the examples (the materials are defined in the
[materials file](usage.qmd#materials-file)):

{{< include _usage-setup.qmd >}}

### 2D hollow-block wall, free-running

A concrete block with one air cavity per cell. The 2D element goes **inside** the
layer stack; finishes are ordinary 1D layers around it. Building the system is
instantaneous (only `solve()` is expensive), so this cell runs live:

```{python}
block = eh.HollowBlock(
    material   = "Concreto",          # single material of the block
    emissivity = 0.9,                 # cavity-wall emissivity (radiation)
    geometry   = {                    # cell measures, in metres
        "web":          0.02,         # half web (rib) thickness
        "block_width":  0.16,         # cavity width
        "cover_top":    0.02,         # outer shell
        "cavity":       0.08,         # cavity height
        "cover_bottom": 0.02,         # inner shell
    },
)

wall2d = eh.System2D(eh.Location(epw_file))
wall2d.tilt = 90                      # walls only (required for HollowBlock)
wall2d.azimuth = 90
wall2d.absortance = 0.6
wall2d.layers = [("Mortero", 0.02), block, ("Yeso", 0.01)]
# 2D stacks accept at most 7 layers INCLUDING the 2D element (fixed slots
# inherited from the C engine); exceeding it raises ValueError. 1D has no limit.
```

The section scheme, to scale — outside on top:

```{python}
wall2d.preview(field="materials");
```

```python
import numpy as np

wall2d.location.meanDay(month=5, year=2025)
wall2d.Tsa()

wall2d.solve()                        # free-running — ~10–20 min (default mesh)
print(wall2d.energy_transfer)         # J/(m²·day), per unit indoor area

# A 2D solve is expensive: SAVE the results, so you pay that time only once.
# solve_dataframe holds Ti, Tso, Tsi, Thueco + the whole Tsa grid;
# Tfield is the (nx, ny) °C field of the last (converged) day.
wall2d.solve_dataframe.to_csv("data/results/hollow_free.csv")
np.save("data/results/hollow_free_Tfield.npy", wall2d.Tfield)
```

Reading the stored files back follows the **same workflow** — same columns, same
plots, no re-solving. That is exactly what this page does (its files were written
by `docs/run_examples.py` with the code above):

```{python}
# The 2D results were computed and saved beforehand by docs/run_examples.py;
# json reads the stored summary (energies, convergence days, runtimes).
import json

RES = "data/results"
summary = json.load(open(f"{RES}/summary.json"))

hollow = pd.read_csv(f"{RES}/hollow_free.csv", index_col=0, parse_dates=True)
s = summary["hollow_free"]
print(f"energy_transfer = {s['energy_transfer']:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {s['energy_transfer']/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)"
      f"  ·  converged in {s['days']} days"
      f"  ·  solve time ≈ {s['runtime_s']/60:.0f} min")
plot_day(hollow, title="Hollow-block wall (2D), east, free-running — May, Cuernavaca")
```

Besides `Ti`, the 2D solver keeps the full **temperature field** of the last
(converged) day — `wall2d.Tfield`, an `(nx, ny)` array in °C on the section mesh,
with the same orientation as `preview()` (outside on top):

```{python}
import numpy as np

T = np.load(f"{RES}/hollow_free_Tfield.npy")
s = summary["hollow_free"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.0, 3.8))
im = ax.imshow(T.T, extent=[0, s["X_mm"], s["Y_mm"], 0], aspect="equal",
               cmap="inferno", interpolation="nearest")
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="T (°C)")
ax.set_xlabel("width [mm]")
ax.set_ylabel("thickness [mm]")
ax.set_title("Tfield — hollow-block wall, end of the converged day", fontsize=10)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```python
wall2d.solveAC()                      # Ti held at Tn

wall2d.solve_dataframe.to_csv("data/results/hollow_ac.csv")   # save, as before
```

```{python}
hollowAC = pd.read_csv(f"{RES}/hollow_ac.csv", index_col=0, parse_dates=True)
s = summary["hollow_ac"]
print(f"cooling_energy = {s['cooling_energy']:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
```

### Joist-and-block roof (`Slab`)

Three solids (compression topping, L-shaped rib, filler block) plus N equal cavities
that can be air (`Fill.AIR`) or a solid fill (`Fill.SOLID`).

```{python}
slab = eh.Slab(
    rib_material     = "ConcretoAltaDensidad",   # joist/rib (L-shaped: web + foot)
    block_material   = "Bovedilla",              # filler block around the cavities
    topping_material = "Concreto",               # compression topping
    fill_type        = eh.Fill.AIR,      # or eh.Fill.SOLID (+ fill_material)
    emissivity       = 0.9,              # required if AIR
    geometry = {
        "web":          0.025,   # rib web
        "foot":         0.025,   # rib foot
        "shoulder":     0.050,   # block between rib and cavities
        "n_cavities":   3,
        "cavity_width": 0.103,
        "topping":      0.100,   # compression topping
        "topping_cap":  0.050,   # topping above the rib web
        "cover_top":    0.030,   # block above the cavity
        "cavity":       0.040,   # cavity height
        "cover_bottom": 0.030,   # block below the cavity
    },
)

roof = eh.System2D(eh.Location(epw_file))
roof.tilt = 0                            # roofs only (required for Slab)
roof.absortance = 0.3
roof.layers = [("Impermeabilizante", 0.003), slab, ("Yeso", 0.015)]
```

```{python}
roof.preview(field="materials");
```

```python
roof.location.meanDay(month=5, year=2025)
roof.Tsa()

roof.solve()                             # or roof.solveAC()

# Same recommendation as with the wall: save, then analyse from the files.
roof.solve_dataframe.to_csv("data/results/slab_free.csv")
np.save("data/results/slab_free_Tfield.npy", roof.Tfield)
```

Recovered from the stored files:

```{python}
slab_df = pd.read_csv(f"{RES}/slab_free.csv", index_col=0, parse_dates=True)
s = summary["slab_free"]
print(f"energy_transfer = {s['energy_transfer']:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {s['energy_transfer']/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)"
      f"  ·  converged in {s['days']} days")
plot_day(slab_df, title="Joist-and-block roof (2D), free-running — May, Cuernavaca")
```

Note how the roof's `Tsa` drops **below** `Ta` at night: that is the long-wave
radiation factor ($RF = 3.9$ °C for horizontal surfaces) at work — the roof sees the
cold sky (see [the 1D model](model-1d.qmd#outdoor-the-sunair-temperature)).

The 2D results go beyond `Ti`: `solve_dataframe` also stores the **surface
temperatures** — `Tso` (outdoor surface), `Tsi` (indoor surface) and `Thueco`
(cavity air) — on the same time grid, plotted here alongside `Ti`:

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.6))
ax.plot(slab_df["Tso"],    color="#eb6834", lw=2, label="Tso (outdoor surface)")
ax.plot(slab_df["Thueco"], color="#9467bd", lw=2, label="Thueco (cavity air)")
ax.plot(slab_df["Tsi"],    color="#0d9488", lw=2, label="Tsi (indoor surface)")
ax.plot(slab_df["Ti"],     color="#2a78d6", lw=2, label="Ti (indoor air)")
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.HourLocator(byhour=[0, 6, 12, 18], tz=slab_df.index.tz))
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%H", tz=slab_df.index.tz))
ax.set_xlabel("hour of the average day")
ax.set_ylabel("temperature (°C)")
ax.set_title("Roof surfaces: the cavity damps the outdoor swing", fontsize=10)
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="upper left")
ax.grid(alpha=0.25, lw=0.5)
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

And its temperature field — note the joists acting as thermal bridges through the
cavity band:

```{python}
T = np.load(f"{RES}/slab_free_Tfield.npy")
s = summary["slab_free"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 3.8))
im = ax.imshow(T.T, extent=[0, s["X_mm"], s["Y_mm"], 0], aspect="equal",
               cmap="inferno", interpolation="nearest")
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="T (°C)")
ax.set_xlabel("width [mm]")
ax.set_ylabel("thickness [mm]")
ax.set_title("Tfield — joist-and-block roof, end of the converged day", fontsize=10)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Filled cavities (`Fill.SOLID`)

The cavity of a `HollowBlock` (or the cavities of a `Slab`) can be filled with a solid
material instead of air — e.g. an insulating core:

```python
block = eh.HollowBlock(
    material      = "Concreto",
    fill_type     = eh.Fill.SOLID,
    fill_material = "EPS",
    geometry      = {"web": 0.02, "block_width": 0.16,
                     "cover_top": 0.02, "cavity": 0.08, "cover_bottom": 0.02},
)
```

Filling with the *same* material as the shell makes the unit homogeneous — equivalent
to a 1D layer (this is one of the package's validation checks).

### Inspecting the section

Before solving you can inspect, **to scale**, how materials and node types are laid
out on the 2D mesh — the section schemes shown with each example above were drawn
by `preview(field="materials")`. `section_report()` prints the verification table:

```{python}
wall2d.section_report()            # table: node types + materials (k, ρc, y-range)
```

The default `preview()` draws three panels: the **node types** (the finite-volume
classification each mesh node gets — interior, cavity walls, corners, air), and the
`k` and `ρc` fields actually assigned to the mesh:

```{python}
wall2d.preview();
```

matplotlib is an optional extra (`pip install enerhabitat[viz]`); without it —
or with `backend="ascii"` — the inspector falls back to a **to-scale ASCII
drawing**, handy on a remote terminal. Note that the drawing is a *resampling* of
the mesh, not the mesh itself: one character is **not** one node — each character
shows the node nearest to its position, and the header states the resolution
(chars vs. mesh nodes, and the size in mm each character covers):

```{python}
roof.preview(field="materials", backend="ascii")
```

The raw arrays are also available: `sec = wall2d.section()` returns the node-type,
`k` and `ρc` fields together with the mesh.

## `config2d` (2D mesh and convergence)

The physics (`La`, `ho`, `hi`, `dt`, air properties) is shared with the global
[`config`](usage.qmd#configuration); `config2d` holds the 2D-only parameters:

| Attribute   | Default | Description |
| ----------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `nx`        | `80`    | mesh nodes across the cell width (adiabatic sides) |
| `ny`        | `160`   | mesh nodes through the thickness (outside → inside) |
| `tol_inner` | `1e-8` °C | inner-step tolerance (max node update **and** max equation residual) |
| `tol_day`   | `5e-4` °C | day-to-day convergence tolerance |
| `max_days`  | `60`    | cap on the day-to-day iterations |
| `max_inner` | `10000` | cap on inner sweeps per step (hit → `converged = False`) |

```python
from enerhabitat import config2d
config2d.nx, config2d.ny = 120, 160
```

> Each solve is single-threaded. For volume (many configurations), parallelise at the
> **process level** — run independent `solve()` calls in separate processes
> (`multiprocessing`, `joblib`); this scales near-linearly (≈6× at 8 processes). See
> [Performance](numerics.qmd#performance).
